chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the foundling, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is free; he is neither sold nor gifted nor sold.'

key_terms.حُرٌّ: Free (as opposed to a slave or property)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a foundling child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the foundling is established as inherently free (hur) rather than property, thereby precluding the commercial transactions of sale or gift (wahb) applicable to slaves. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that the status of freedom is intrinsic to the foundling, distinguishing them from chattel in Islamic law. It reflects the broader principle of preserving lineage and dignity, ensuring the child is not commodified by the finder or the state.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the found (abandoned child). So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Free. He can neither be sold nor gifted’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “
I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a discarded child. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is free but cannot be sold or given away as a gift.’”
